**Answer**: You can usually make widgets easier to click by increasing the padding of their container in `styles.css`, so the clickable area is larger than just the text/icon itself.

Even though the weather widget isn’t shown in the snippets, all widgets share the same basic styling rules described in `docs/Styling.md`:

- Widgets get a widget‑specific class like `.clock-widget`, `.media-widget`, etc. (see example under **Generic Widget Style** and **Widget Container Styling**: `.clock-widget .widget-container { … }`, `.media-widget .widget-container { … }`).  
- The clickable area is the container around the icon/text: `.widget-container`.  
  (Lines under “Widget Container Styling” mention: “Each icon and text is wrapped in a container. This container can be styled with the following: `.widget-container`.”)

So for your weather widget you can:

1. Find its widget class name  
   In your config (`config.yaml` or similar), it will be defined as a widget, commonly resulting in a class like `.weather-widget`. If you’re unsure of the exact class, you can temporarily style all widgets as a test (see step 3).

2. Open or create `styles.css`  
   As per `docs/Styling.md`, YASB loads styles from `styles.css` in your config directory.

3. Add padding to the widget container  

   If you know the class (example: `.weather-widget`):

   ```css
   .weather-widget .widget-container {
       padding: 6px 10px; /* increase vertical & horizontal clickable area */
   }
   ```

   If you’re not sure of the widget’s specific class yet, test on all widgets:

   ```css
   .widget .widget-container {
       padding: 6px 10px;
   }
   ```

   Then narrow it down once you confirm it works.

4. Optionally add margin/rounding so it feels more like a button:

   ```css
   .weather-widget .widget-container {
       padding: 6px 12px;
       margin: 2px 4px;
       border-radius: 6px;
   }
   ```

Because the click handling is bound to the container that wraps the icon/label, increasing the container’s padding makes the whole “button” area clickable, not just the center text/icon.

About which widget are you talking? Is that problem with the apps widget?
